_comment: Hand-curated deals tracker shown on the Deals page. Not written by the pipeline: edit by hand. Every deal must carry at least one primary source (company release, SEC filing or regulator) and a 'verified' date; scripts/test_deals.mjs enforces the rules below in CI and the page hides any entry that breaks them. Status follows what a source says: a deal stays 'pending' until a source confirms completion. Sizes are as the source states them; usd_bn is set only when a source gives a US dollar figure, and is never converted here.
scope: Signed or completed transactions involving Bermuda life & annuity reinsurers, their sponsors and their cedants, announced or completed since 1 January 2025.
vetting: At least one primary source: the company's own release, an SEC filing, or a regulator document.
Facts on the card (parties, size, dates, status) come from those sources; independent coverage is linked where it adds detail.
A deal is listed only once it is signed. Reports of talks or exploratory sales are left out until a party confirms them.
Status is 'Closed' only when a primary source confirms completion (an announcement that a deal will close doesn't count); until then it stays 'Pending', and the card says when it was last checked.

deals.title: Talcott reinsures $6.3bn of Lincoln Financial GUL and funding agreements
deals.summary: A Talcott subsidiary reinsures about $5.8bn of in-force guaranteed universal life statutory reserves (about 37% of Lincoln's remaining GUL block) plus about $500m of funding agreement business, partly as coinsurance with funds withheld and partly as modco. Lincoln keeps administration and put the all-in statutory capital impact at about $200m. With its 2023 Fortitude Re deal, about 60% of Lincoln's GUL block is now reinsured.

Dayforward's insurance entities and legacy policies are excluded. Gives Fortitude Re its own annuity origination platform.

deals.title: Unum reinsures $3.4bn of long-term care reserves with Fortitude Re

size.text: $3.4bn individual LTC statutory reserves + ~$120m IDI in-force premium

deals.summary: Unum America cedes to Fortitude Reinsurance Company Ltd. on a coinsurance basis, effective 1 Jan 2025: $3.4bn of individual long-term care statutory reserves (19% of Unum's LTC statutory reserves) and a quota share of multi-life individual disability business (about $120m of in-force premium, 20% of Unum US IDI premium). deals.title: Fortitude Re to reinsure a further $3.8bn of Unum's individual LTC
deals.summary: Unum America will recapture about 50,000 individual long-term care policies from its captive Fairwind Insurance Company and cede them to Fortitude Reinsurance Company Ltd. on a coinsurance basis. The block carries $3.8bn of statutory reserves (about $4.5bn best estimate), which is 26% of Unum's total LTC statutory reserves and 52% of its individual LTC reserves. Fortitude Re will retrocede 100% of the LTC insurance risk to a highly rated global reinsurer and keep only the spread-based risk. Unum keeps administration, including claims and premium rate increase management. Together with the 2025 Fortitude Re deal, the transaction cuts Unum's total LTC statutory reserves by about 40%.
deals.note: Closing expected during 2026, subject to regulatory approvals; the 8-K says the coinsurance agreement signed at closing will be effective 1 Apr 2026. No completion announcement found as of 20 Oct 2026.
